liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Scarlet>Fire is the high point, with growling Hammond from Brent and heavy, clear Phil; Scarlet>Fire features strong Jerry and Brent interplay, with Brent driving it with Hammond licks [8][9][10]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Althea and Let It Grow are singled out as strong first-set highlights; Garcia's leads in Let It Grow, Fire, Spanish Jam and The Other One are on the money [13][17]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Brent can be heard shouting over Bobby's vocals [7]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's is electric, with Garcia singing confidently and proudly [15]
- **Passenger** (1 review): Passenger features random Phil bombs bursting throughout [15]
- **Althea** (1 review): Jerry plays shredding, fiery guitar on Althea [7]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): Garcia plays scorching leads throughout Fire, considered among the best versions [13]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): The Spanish Jam sounds very Spanish and leads into a bossa-flavored Other One [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-10-19.131801.mtx-fix.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 172 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd81-10-19.sbd.macdonald.7914.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 4.13/5 by 15 [3]. Said about its sound: A nice soundboard, though the tape quality is held back by some flaw; reviewer would otherwise give five stars; Brent is very forward in the mix, while Bobby is almost absent; Soundboard hiss is somewhat distracting but not enough to spoil the show [8][9][12][17]
- **gd1981-10-19.sbd.miller.95781.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 3.82/5 by 11 [4]. Said about its sound: The mix is a mess, and Phil is missing from it for the first few songs [4]
- **gd1981-10-19.stankiewicz.patched.131522.flac1644**: soundboard; 21 songs; 171 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer speculates Garcia played his best in the country of his ancestors [15]
- Reviewer thinks it is probably not the best show of the European tour, though worth hearing [7]
- Reviewer sees it as the end of an era, just before the sloppy mid-1980s period [12]
- Overshadowed by the classic 10-16-1981 show that came before it [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-10-19.131801.mtx-fix.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 source matrix by Dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:095781) Recording Info: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN; Transfer Info: SHN ->… [1]. Also: Matrix source, FLAC 16-bit, with show information embedded in each file's header; tags are lost if converted to wav [1]
- **gd81-10-19.sbd.macdonald.7914.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1981-10-19.sbd.miller.95781.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD -> EAC ->SHN [4]. Also: This is a clean-up of shnid 7914, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones; The tape flip between Space and Drums was cleaned up with a crossfade; the set 2 disc change is seamless [4]
- **gd1981-10-19.stankiewicz.patched.131522.flac1644**: taped by Richie Stankiewicz; transferred by Richie Stankiewicz; source: Source: Beyer M-160>Sony TC-D5M. Transfer 1st set: MAC > Sony TC-K3es > USBPre2. Transfer 2nd set: 1st Gen > Sony TC-K3es > USBPre2. Recorded center directly… [2]
